author: @jeremyfowers

evidence.api_compatibility: No API changes. Only documentation files were modified. The change does not alter any server behavior, configuration schema, CLI contract, or persistence format.
evidence.documentation: The change is itself a documentation fix, and it is well-scoped. It replaces incorrect instructions (open HTML files directly from disk) with correct ones (serve over localhost with explanation of why). Both affected files are in examples/ and the new instructions reference the exact HTML files users would want. The prose is clear and includes the specific localhost URLs users should open.
evidence.manual_release_testing: No human exercised the updated documentation instructions end-to-end. The change directs users to a user-reachable surface (running python3 -m http.server in an examples directory and opening demo HTML pages in a browser). Nothing in the PR description, comments, or CI logs shows this path was tested with the live server. The documentation text is internally correct -- file:// does trigger Origin: null, which the server rejects -- but manual verification against the current build is warranted before shipping.
evidence.post_approval_commits: No commits were added to the PR branch after the latest approval. Single commit e0e01c1, authored by Claude with co-authorship by the PR author, was approved at 16:00Z and 16:39Z and merged at 20:07Z. The merge commit 421eabdf is the squash/merge of that single commit.
evidence.review: PR #3547 was authored by @jeremyfowers and approved by @abn (submitted at 2026-09-11T16:00:15Z with 'LGTM') and @superm1 (MEMBER, approved at 2026-09-11T16:39:17Z). @abn's subject area includes telemetry, sandboxing, and HTTP, making them a qualified reviewer for this change that addresses the server's allowed_origins behavior. @superm1 (MEMBER, subject area includes security, ROCm, linux packaging) also approved. There were no post-approval commits. Codex (automated bot) raised a valid inline comment suggesting adding --bind 127.0.0.1 to keep the HTTP server local and avoid exposing the filesystem to other network hosts; superm1 acknowledged the comment with a laugh emoji but the PR merged without addressing it. The security concern is mild (users typically run this in a terminal in a known folder), but it is a legitimate tightening that the reviewers did not pursue.
evidence.security: Codex identified that python3 -m http.server binds to all interfaces by default, so running the command in an arbitrary folder could expose that folder's contents to the local network. The PR merged without adding --bind 127.0.0.1. The risk is low since users are expected to run this in a controlled examples directory in a terminal they control, but tightening the instruction would remove the exposure entirely. No other security concerns.
evidence.tests: This is a documentation-only change (2 markdown files: examples/README.md and examples/debate-arena.md), so there are no code tests affected. All CI checks that ran for this PR passed, including Docs And Style, markdown-link-check, backend-docs-drift, and CodeQL across all languages. No tests were weakened or deleted.

maintainer_todos.text: Start the Lemonade server, serve the HTML examples with python3 -m http.server 8080 from an examples directory, and confirm the demo pages load and communicate with the server as described.

subject: Serve example HTML demos over localhost instead of opening from disk (#3547)
summary: Updates two documentation files to instruct users to serve example HTML demos over a local HTTP server instead of opening them directly from disk, which the server's default allowed_origins policy rejects.
verdict_reason: All CI checks passed, two substantive approvals landed, but no evidence shows anyone manually verified the updated documentation instructions against the live server.
